items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-06-14
items.q: At that time, they had Vernon Castle doing the castle walk.

ctx.x: And they're saying there was some part of the creation of jazz. That Jack Lane, who played a drum and lousy drums at that, created jazz. Now that's good enough for men who thrive on thievery, on a word that we had nothing to do. Our jazz was started in Chicago. We took in the ragtime and changed the rhythm in Chicago. In 1916, we seen we were going to be a flop the first night. And I, being a good dancer, I watched those people. At that time, they had Vernon Castle doing the castle walk. And everybody was trying…

No, I wrote that mostly as a sort of, you might say, editor. Walter Allen managed to interview the various musicians that were still living. And he sent me the facts and I wrote them, sewed them up together. I was more concerned with the records than with the legends. I wasn't very interested in these obscure people from the shadows who were said to have played with this, that and the other musician, in this, that and the other band, and who never made any records at all. I'm not interested in music I can't hear…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: We developed it there by watching these people who were trying to imitate Vine and Castle doing the castle walk

ctx.x: In other words, the band went up there more...
We developed it there by watching these people who were trying to imitate Vine and Castle doing the castle walk, which was a one step.
I see. So in other words, you didn't even leave New Orleans as a jazz band. You went up there as actually a dance band.
